Title: Diagnosis of test `test_getPackageName_Class`

Details:
The test `test_getPackageName_Class` calls the method `ClassUtils.getPackageName` with `String[].class` and expects the result to be `"java.lang"`. This indicates that the method should correctly handle array classes by deriving the package name from the array's element type.

The `getPackageName(Class<?> cls)` implementation first checks if `cls` is `null`, and returns an empty string if so. If not null, it calls `getPackageName(String className)` with `cls.getName()`.

The `getPackageName(String className)` method accepts the class name in a string form and tries to extract the package name by finding the last occurrence of the package separator character `'.'`. It returns the substring before the last dot or an empty string if none is present. However, there is a comment indicating "Strip array encoding" and "Strip Object type encoding" but no actual stripping logic is present. 

Java class names for arrays are represented in a special internal form like `[Ljava.lang.String;` for `String[]`. As the code stands, `getPackageName` just looks for the last `'.'` in this representation, which it likely does not find because of the encoding (or finds a dot unrelated to the package separator). This means the method will either return an empty string or an incorrect package name for array classes.

The absence of logic to strip the array encoding (e.g., the leading `[L` and trailing `;`) from the class name string is the root cause of the test failure. The method does not handle class names representing arrays properly, leading to returning an empty string or wrong package names instead of the correct `"java.lang"` for `String[].class`.

Thus, the missing processing for array type encoding in `ClassUtils.getPackageName(String)` caused the test failure.

Suggested locations for fix:
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getPackageName(java.lang.String)  
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getPackageName(java.lang.Class<?>)
